title: Input/Output Imbalance Mitigation — Variant Exploration for Per-Token Hosted Pricing
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: a non-trivial portion of hosted API usage shows extreme input/output token imbalance (e.g., retrieval-heavy customers with high input tokens and short generated outputs). Current per-token IO billing creates perceived unfairness for these customers and drives negotiation friction in enterprise SQs (security questionnaire + contract clauses) and committed-reserved conversations. Goal: explore and validate practical pricing variants that reduce customer churn and sales friction while preserving unit economics and not materially degrading revenue for comparable workloads.

Hypotheses: 
1) A small directional delta (output price = input price * 1.15) reduces perceived overbilling for retrieval-heavy flows and will increase conversion on enterprise SQ negotiations by >= 10% without >3% revenue degradation across cohort. 
2) Session-anchored minimums (short-session credit buckets) will improve churn for low-duration, high-input customers and reduce billing disputes. 
3) Telemetry-driven dynamic adjustment (per-customer IO ratio threshold that toggles a small credit) can be safe if rolled out to beta customers and limited by monthly cap.

Variants to test (detailed):
- Variant A: Symmetric single-token price (no IO split) with preserved streaming surcharge. Baseline for fairness perception.
- Variant B: Directional weighting: output tokens billed at 1.15x input tokens. Apply only to hosted API public plans, opt-in for enterprise.
- Variant C: Session Anchor Credit: sessions under 10s OR <256 output tokens receive a per-session credit that offsets first N input tokens per session. Intended for short retrieval flows.
- Variant D: Telemetry Toggle: per-customer rule that applies a 5% credit when monthly aggregate IO ratio (input/output) exceeds 4:1; capped at $2k/mo. Requires telemetry + billing gating.

Success metrics and guardrails: 
- Primary metrics: enterprise SQ sign-off rate on pricing appendices, trial->paid conversion for trial customers with high IO ratio, net revenue retention change for affected cohorts.
- Safety guards: early canary to <0.5% of revenue; automated rollback if MRR delta > -5% in first 7 days; monitor cost-per-token delta using runtime telemetry (ENG telemetry dashboard).

Rollout plan: 
1) Design experiment: create billing simulator with sampled telemetry from last 6 months (data ops + infra run). (owner: Data & Pricing infra)
2) Legal/Sales & SQ alignment: produce a short addendum template describing directional weighting and session credits; feed into security questionnaire responses. (owner: Legal, Sales Eng)
3) Canary: expose Variant B and C as opt-in beta on hosted plans (beta flag behind account settings + explicit contract language for enterprise). 1 week canary -> 4 week extended beta. (owner: PM + Billing)
4) Evaluate: use dashboards for revenue delta, conversion lift, and support ticket volume. Decision gate at end of beta for broader rollout.

Telemetry & instrumentation required: 
- Per-session IO ratio (session_id, ingress_tokens, egress_tokens) aggregation in product telemetry.
- Billing simulator outputs mapped to accounting revenue buckets.
- Support tag for 'IO-pricing-dispute' to surface disputes quickly.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- Complexity vs transparency: customers prefer simple per-token bills, but small directional rules can be easier to explain in contract language than per-session credits.
- Implementation cost: Variant D (telemetry toggle) requires new per-customer billing rules and gating; higher engineering cost and longer lead time.
- Enterprise fairness: enterprise customers with negotiated commits may demand carve-outs; need to add explicit language in SQ/contract templates.

Next steps (short-term): 
- 2025-02-01: run billing simulator for all top-100 accounts by spend (Data lead: Priya Desai).
- 2025-02-07: draft SQ addendum and run Legal review (owner: Emma Cho, Legal).
- 2025-02-12: engineering estimation for billing rules and console UI changes (owner: ENG infra).
- 2025-02-20: kickoff opt-in beta (expected cohort: 200 accounts).

- Pricing RFC / simulator notebook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PRIC/Input-Output+Imbalance+RFC
- Billing simulator repo & sample outputs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-sim/pull/87

- Support triage checklist (proto): https://docs.redwood.com/support/triage/io_pricing_disputes.md

Stakeholder feedback (summary of comments in review):
- Sales (Teresa Liu): positive on Variant B as it matches many competitor patterns; requests clear per-customer examples for EMEA accounts.
- Legal (Emma Cho): wants 'no-implicit-reprice' language and a maximum monthly cap clause for any telemetry-driven credits.
- Finance (Omar Rahman): asks for a modeled P&L for the top-10 impacted accounts and stress scenarios if IO ratios shift further.
- UX (Lola Okafor): suggests a single new line item in billing UI labelled 'Session credits / IO adjustment' rather than splitting many micro-lines.
Comments and updates: 2025-01-10 — Initial spike completed: sampled 30K sessions; median IO ratio for retrieval flows = 5.6:1. (Ava)
2025-01-20 — Finance P&L pass done; preliminary revenue impact for Variant B estimated -1.8% on sampled cohort. (Omar)
2025-01-28 — Legal provided clause template and requested cap wording. (Emma)
2025-02-05 — Engineering estimates: Variant A/B/C ~ 3 wks infra work; Variant D requires ~8 wks and new billing rule engine. (Eng infra)
2025-02-12 — PM review: prioritize Variant B + C for beta; defer Variant D to post-beta. Approved by GTM. (Ronan)
2025-02-14 — Beta cohort onboarding scripts and opt-in flow drafted. (Ava)
2025-02-15 — Ready for canary gating and observability dashboard hookup. (Owner: Ronan)
decision_log: 2025-02-12 — Decision: run Variant B (directional weighting) + Variant C (session anchor) in opt-in beta. Rationale: best tradeoff of implementation effort vs impact on sales friction.
2025-02-14 — Decision: postpone Variant D (telemetry toggle) to post-beta to avoid long engineering lead and complex SQ language.
2025-02-15 — Rollout guard: canary limited to accounts <0.5% revenue exposure and explicit opt-in for enterprise trials.
